input.quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 10 is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere (Section 6 termination rights are mutual for convenience and breach, not change of control), so no Vendor exit right needs deletion. The clause is mutual and applies a reasonableness standard to consent, but it subjects every assignment, including an assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to the Contractor's prior consent. That fails the fallback requirement of a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, so we have added that carve-out only, leaving the existing consent and reasonableness mechanics (which already satisfy the remaining fallback elements) untouched.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
ops.newText: Except for assignment to a successor upon written notice to the other party, neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have carved out assignment to a successor on written notice, so neither party is locked in on a corporate transaction; all other assignments still require consent that is not unreasonably withheld. This reflects our fallback assignment position.
proposal.summary: Add mutual successor-assignment carve-out with written notice to the nonassignability clause.
